text:
Nina: Heads up — partner X is migrating traffic to our eu-west-1 staging cluster tomorrow. They sent a dry-run schedule that looks like a ~2.5x delta for a 3-hour window starting 08:00 UTC. Can we confirm autoscaler guardrails?
Sam: Ack. Which fleet/model are they hitting?
Nina: Primary go-to is gen-13-small on dedicated pool 'eu-west-gpu-a'. Fallback path routes to quantized gen-13-q4.
Priya: 2.5x for 3h will blow past our burst cap if steady_min remains at current 12 GPUs. We set burst_cap = 1.25x historically.
Marco: We intentionally kept burst conservative because of regional power/capacity limits in eu-west racks. If we bump burst too high we risk noisy neighbor throttles.
Clara: Is this a hard SLA for the partner, or can we use degraded quality fallback (quantized model) if capacity tight?
Nina: Partner expects near-prod perf for dry-run, but will accept degraded if we flag it. They prefer predictable failure modes over slowness.
Sam: Proposed quick plan: temporarily raise burst_cap to 1.6x for the 3-hour window, add a hard spend cap of $X/hr for that pool, and enable immediate fallback to gen-13-q4 at 120s latency threshold. Also alerting to paging if queue length > 50.
Priya: I like the spend cap + fallback. Can we implement as a short-lived policy in autoscaler? Example patch: 
```yaml
autoscaler:
  pools:
    - name: eu-west-gpu-a
      steady_min: 12
      steady_max: 48
      burst_multiplier: 1.6   # temp for dry-run
      burst_window: 10800    # 3h in seconds
      spend_limit_per_hour: "$2500"
      fallback_model: gen-13-q4
```
Marco: That patch looks good. Two operational checks: 1) network egress quotas for that rack, 2) ensure kernel image with q4 quant works on older instance types.
Clara: Who will run the change and monitor? I can push policy, but need someone to watch for paging and runbacks.
Nina: Clara + Sam to deploy policy. Priya to coordinate cost approval. Marco to do a quick instance-compat smoke in staging now. I'll inform the partner of our plan.
ops-bot: scheduled policy update by @Clara at 2026-03-20T07:15:00Z (dry-run window: 2026-03-20T08:00:00Z — 11:00:00Z)
deploy-bot: deploy started: autoscaler-config/eu-west-gpu-a@rev-82 by Clara
Sam: Monitoring checks to watch during the window — token throughput, GPU util, queue depth, tail latency, and cost burn rate. I've added a temporary dashboard and a runbook snippet.
Sam: Runbook snippet: 
1) If queue depth > 200 for > 2m -> escalate to oncall.
2) If spend_rate > 110% of spend_limit for 10m -> rollback burst_multiplier to 1.25x and switch routing to fallback model.
3) If network error rate > 3% -> throttle inbound and engage cloud-nets.
Priya: Cost note: estimated incremental GPU-hours = (48-12)*3 = 108 GPU-hours max, ~estimate $1.2k for the window if fully utilized. Confirmed with finance headroom.
Marco: Smoke passed on quantized image on a T4-equivalent instance, env var set: `REDWOOD_FORCE_Q4=true` toggles fallback locally.
Clara: Patch applied, monitoring live, alerts wired. Keeping channel open during the window.
Nina: Thanks all — will close once partner confirms dry-run traffic completed and metrics look ok.
Sam: Postmortem (quick): capture actual GPU-hours, peak queue, and any tail-latency regressions; feed into next quarter's capacity forecast.
Nina: Closing note: we should consider a pre-authorized "surge token" for strategic partners to avoid manual policy changes next time. Filed an RFC. :memo:
